prisoner.name: Michael Zaharibu Dorrough
prisoner.description: Michael Zaharibu Dorrough, legally Michael Reed Dorrough, is a California prison writer and organizer against prolonged solitary confinement. His correspondence describes participation in the 2013 hunger strike at Corcoran. Supporters say he eventually left long-term isolation following the 2015 settlement over California’s segregation policies. His current CDCR listing, checked September 10, 2026, places him at the Substance Abuse Treatment Facility and State Prison, Corcoran. The case here concerns continued segregation associated with political reading and contested classification evidence; it does not describe his earlier murder and narcotics conviction as an activism prosecution.

cases.charges: Continued administrative segregation after a disputed 2006 gang-status review
cases.sentence: In the 2012 UN petition, Dorrough said a 2006 review extended his SHU confinement using political and historical books as evidence. The submission describes actual ongoing isolation years after that review. His later published letters also document confinement at Corcoran SHU during 2013 and 2014. The claimed political basis is his account, not a judicial finding. This was prison classification within an existing sentence, not a new criminal conviction. No exact end date is established for this episode.

case_research.custody_evidence: Sources describe actual multi-year segregation linked to political materials or prison organizing. This is separate from the underlying criminal sentence. The final exit date for the specific episode is not verified.

entries.custody_evidence: Actual prolonged segregation documented, with political motive attributed where disputed. Current imprisonment independently matched through CDCR. No assumption that the documented segregation continues today.

prisoner.name: Todd Lewis Ashker
prisoner.description: Todd Lewis Ashker is a California prison organizer who helped build the movement against indefinite solitary confinement and was a lead plaintiff in Ashker v. Brown. His work included hunger-strike organizing and the cross-racial Agreement to End Hostilities. After the 2015 settlement, he challenged renewed isolation as retaliation for his advocacy. California legislative records summarize a 2023 court finding in his favor on that issue. CDCR listed him at California Men’s Colony on September 10, 2026. The case below concerns retaliation within prison, separately from his underlying criminal sentence.

cases.charges: Retaliatory administrative segregation connected to prison-rights litigation and organizing
cases.sentence: California’s March 2025 Assembly hearing agenda reports that, on January 5, 2023, the court found CDCR had retaliated against Ashker by holding him in administrative segregation since 2017 despite approval for general-population housing. It directed the parties to discuss remedies. This documents years of actual confinement, not a proposed penalty. The final segregation exit date remains unverified. Later appellate proceedings concerning broader settlement monitoring are distinct from this historical finding; no present solitary-confinement status is inferred.

prisoner.name: Mutope Duguma
prisoner.aka: James Daren Crawford; James Darren Crawford
prisoner.description: Mutope Duguma, identified by CDCR as James Daren Crawford, is a New Afrikan writer and participant in California’s prisoner hunger-strike movement. He has argued that officials used his political beliefs to justify prolonged isolation under a gang classification he disputed. In June 2012, the California Court of Appeal upheld his right to send a political letter to the San Francisco Bay View; that decision concerned censorship and did not release him from prison. CDCR listed him at California State Prison, Los Angeles County on September 10, 2026. The case recorded here concerns segregation within his earlier criminal sentence.

cases.charges: Prolonged SHU confinement under a disputed Black Guerrilla Family associate classification
cases.sentence: Duguma’s 2012 UN petition account and correspondence published by Solitary Watch describe more than a decade in segregation. He denied gang involvement and said officials used his political beliefs and another prisoner’s claim to justify isolation. The sources establish prolonged confinement, but the political motive remains attributed to him. Reports differ on the full historical duration, so no exact continuous term or ongoing solitary-confinement counter is assigned. The separate 2012 mail-censorship victory is not a segregation release order.

prisoner.name: Joka Heshima Jinsai
prisoner.aka: Shannon Lemar Denham; Shannon Heshima Denham; S. Heshima Denham
prisoner.description: Joka Heshima Jinsai, legally Shannon Lemar Denham, is an incarcerated writer and community organizer associated with the Autonomous Infrastructure Mission and the campaign to end the Thirteenth Amendment’s punishment exception. His supporters describe work on community food, education and economic initiatives. He has challenged prolonged segregation linked to political expression. CDCR listed him at Kern Valley State Prison on September 10, 2026. The case below concerns that prison segregation rather than classifying his original criminal prosecution as activism-related custody.

cases.charges: Prolonged SHU confinement based on disputed political-material and association evidence
cases.sentence: Denham’s account in the 2012 UN petition describes about eleven years of segregation and says officials relied on political artwork, a prison-news article and association evidence. A later clemency campaign also reports prolonged isolation connected to his advocacy. These are attributed accounts, not a finding that every classification allegation was false. The reviewed sources do not establish a reliable exact endpoint for this episode. No parole estimate or transfer out of isolation is entered as a prison release date.

research_notes: Existing identities are skipped in full. No existing biographies, fields, cases or portraits are modified. All four are currently listed in custody; this is not proof they remain in the historical segregation described here. Case dates and numeric durations deliberately remain blank because the model would otherwise extend an open-ended segregation case to today. Current CDCR admission dates and parole eligibility dates are not substituted. Three exact DOBs come from the named petition accounts and agree with current CDCR ages; Denham’s reported 1960 DOB conflicts with current age 54 and is withheld. No deaths verified. Only two verified personal support websites are populated. Coordinates are approximate communities of current listed custody, not exact cell locations. Historical Corcoran SHU is not the separate current SATF facility. Original convictions are context, not new activism cases. Remaining leads are retained in the audit; continue to Black Liberation Army next.
